hints: Use the binomial theorem to find the general term for $x^3$ in $(3+ax)^6$.
walkthrough:
Identify the $x^3$ term in the binomial expansion of $(3+ax)^6$:
$$\text{Term in } x^3 = \binom{6}{3}(3)^3(ax)^3 = 20 \times 27 \times a^3 x^3 = 540a^3 x^3$$

Equate the coefficient of $x^3$ to 160:
$$540a^3 = 160 \implies a^3 = \frac{160}{540} = \frac{16}{54} = \frac{8}{27}$$

Take the cube root to find the exact value of $a$:
$$a = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8}{27}} = \frac{2}{3}$$

hints: Find the $x^2$ term in the expansion of $(3+ax)^6$ with $a = \frac{2}{3}$.
Determine the combinations that produce $x^3$ when multiplying by $(1-2x)$: $(x^3 \text{ term}) \times 1$ and $(x^2 \text{ term}) \times (-2x)$.
Calculate $160(1) + 540(-2)$ to obtain the final coefficient.
walkthrough:
Find the $x^2$ term in the expansion of $(3+\frac{2}{3}x)^6$:
$$\text{Term in } x^2 = \binom{6}{2}(3)^4\left(\frac{2}{3}x\right)^2 = 15 \times 81 \times \frac{4}{9}x^2 = 15 \times 9 \times 4 x^2 = 540x^2$$

Identify all products forming an $x^3$ term in the expansion of $(3+\frac{2}{3}x)^6(1-2x)$:
$$\text{From } (160x^3)(1) = 160x^3$$
$$\text{From } (540x^2)(-2x) = -1080x^3$$

Sum the coefficients to determine the total coefficient of $x^3$:
$$\text{Coefficient of } x^3 = 160 - 1080 = -920$$
